messages:
kira: Heads-up: premerge SAST + DAST bundle for feature/telemetry is blocked. Scanner uploads failing and DAST shows a potential auth bypass on /internal/metrics.

tom: Error from scanner-agent: 
```
time="2026-07-11T09:12:03Z" level=error msg="upload failed" err="rpc error: code=PermissionDenied desc=kms:Decrypt denied for resource projects/keystore/cryptoKeys/ci-fixture-key"
```

sami: We pushed an orgwide RBAC tweak yesterday (infra PR 6018). I think the umbrella binding for scanner service accounts was replaced with per-key bindings and one of the fixture keys was omitted.

infra-bot: Detected IAM change in PR 6018 by infra-ci at 2026-07-11T02:05Z. Delta: removed member serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com from roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on resource projects/keystore/cryptoKeys/ci-fixture-key.

kira: That explains the KMS failures. But the DAST auth-bypass is weird: app logs show a 200 when scanner hits /internal/metrics with header X-Internal: yes, but normal users get 403.

tom: Two possibilities: (A) ingress intentionally white-lists X-Internal for internal scanners and RBAC change removed an upstream validation step, or (B) scanner identity is being mistaken for an elevated role because of header injection.

sami: We added a header-forwarding rule in PR 5992 earlier this month to support scanners. Maybe the interplay with the RBAC change created a gap. We should not suppress the DAST finding until we have audit evidence.

sec-bot: Audit scan: request_id=req-11b2c -> incoming request from scanner@redwood-ci returned 200 at 2026-07-11T09:11:59Z. No matching audit log found in audit-sink for that request_id. Also, keystore IAM change recorded at 2026-07-11T02:05Z.

kira: Immediate plan: (1) block any suppression approvals for sup-id sup-2203, (2) issue ephemeral kms:Decrypt to let SAST uploads finish so CI doesn't backlog, (3) perform a manual DAST run with --trace to capture request headers and request_id, (4) enable ingress-level request logging to audit-sink for 24h.

sec-oncall: I'm authorizing an ephemeral grant for scanner@redwood-ci: /grant kms:Decrypt scanner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com duration=15m audit_id=GNT-610a1. Captured in audit. Do not merge infra changes until follow-ups are open.

infra-bot: Ephemeral grant issued, expiry scheduled at 2026-07-11T09:27:03Z. Audit entry id=GNT-610a1 attached. CI notified.

tom: Re-running the failing SAST jobs now. Uploads resumed, artifacts available. DAST runner started with verbose trace: 
```
# run locally simulating scanner identity
dast-runner --target https://staging.redwood.internal --endpoint /internal/metrics --impersonate scanner@redwood-ci --trace
```

sami: While uploads are unblocked, I'm opening infra/PR-6023 to (A) add the missing fixture binding with narrow scope, (B) add an infra smoke-check that runs a kms:Decrypt probe as part of pre-merge, and (C) update the rollout checklist to require "consumer smoke run" for any keystore IAM change.

sec-bot: Ticket SEC-5202 created: "keystore RBAC change caused scanner uploads + DAST audit gaps" assigned to sami, severity P1. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/SEC-5202. Audit slice attached.

kira: Results from the DAST verbose trace: request headers include X-Internal: yes injected by ingress-router; app accepted it and returned 200. However, the request had a scanner identity and the authN path did not emit an audit entry for the pre-auth check. That missing audit log is the gating condition for suppression.

sami: Root cause hypothesis: the keystore RBAC change made us rely more on header-based trust for scanner flows to reduce KMS calls; when the binding was tightened the authN flow short-circuited and forgot to write the audit event. That's a telemetry bug + RBAC collision.

sec-oncall: Follow-ups required before any suppression: (1) restore audit emission for the authN check and backfill missing entries if possible, (2) revert or patch PR 6018 to re-add the fixture binding until infra smoke passes, (3) add a fatal pre-merge gate that runs the kms probe and validates audit emission, (4) add an alert that fires when an ingress header that enables internal access is present in a 200 response without a corresponding audit-sink entry.

infra-bot: PR 6023 opened by sami to re-add binding and smoke check. Link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6023. Marked must-pass.

sec-bot: Ephemeral grant expired at 2026-07-11T09:27:03Z. No further KMS AccessDenied events observed after PR-6023 was queued and the probe passed in CI.

kira: I've attached the DAST trace and artifact bundle to SEC-5202. Suppression is blocked pending audit backfill and a security reviewer sign-off.

sami: I'll also add a small integration test in the scanner runner that asserts audit-sink emission for any request that triggers internal routes; that will fail CI if we ever regress again.

sec-oncall: Closing this Slack incident thread. SEC-5202 remains open until infra PR 6023 merges and the audit backfill is validated. If anyone sees the sup-id sup-2203 attempted, ping sec-oncall with the request_id. Thanks."
